purpose: Interferon Gamma-1B is used to help reduce the number and severity of serious infections in people with a rare immune condition called chronic granulomatous disease (CGD). It is also used to slow down the worsening of a serious bone condition called severe malignant osteopetrosis. Think of it as a medicine that helps boost and fine-tune your immune system so your body can better fight off harmful germs.
how_it_works: Your body naturally makes a protein called interferon gamma that helps your immune system fight infections. This medicine is a man-made version of that same protein. When you inject it, it helps certain immune cells become stronger and more active, making them better at finding and destroying bacteria and other harmful invaders.
common_side_effects: Flu-like symptoms such as fever, chills, headache, muscle aches, and tiredness are the most common side effects, especially right after your injection. You may also notice redness, soreness, or swelling at the injection site. These effects often get better over time as your body gets used to the medicine.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you develop chest pain, trouble breathing, confusion, or signs of a serious infection. This medicine can sometimes affect your heart, liver, kidneys, or nervous system, so your doctor will do regular blood tests to monitor you. Do not use this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant unless your doctor specifically advises it. Always store it in the refrigerator and never shake the vial.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection), usually three times a week — for example on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. The exact dose is based on your body size and your specific condition. Your healthcare team will teach you or a caregiver how to inject it at home safely.
